svg.aria-label: Delayed puberty sorted by LH and FSH: high LH and FSH means failed gonads such as Turner or Klinefelter syndrome and the next step is a karyotype; low LH and FSH means constitutional delay with a delayed bone age, functional hypogonadotropism from low leptin, Kallmann syndrome with anosmia, or another central cause
svg.text: Late puberty: LH and FSH sort the cause, then the bone age
No breast bud by age 13, or testes under 4 mL by age 14
Measure LH and FSH, and get a bone age X-ray
LH and FSH high: gonads failed
Turner syndrome (45,X)
Streak ovaries, short stature
No breast development
Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY)
Small, firm testes
Tall, long legs
Chemotherapy or radiation
Damaged ovaries or testes
Next step: karyotype
LH and FSH low: the axis is quiet
Constitutional delay: the most common cause
Healthy, short, a parent who matured late
Bone age delayed about 2 years
Low LH and FSH fit the bone age; it starts on its own
Functional: low leptin suppresses GnRH pulses
Anorexia, hard training, chronic illness
Treat the cause: restore energy balance
Kallmann syndrome
GnRH neurons fail to migrate from the olfactory placode
Anosmia: loss of smell; normal karyotype
Other central causes
Pituitary mass, prolactin excess, hypothyroidism
Check TSH and prolactin; MRI if suspected
Bone age is delayed in every cause; the LH and FSH level picks the next test.
